choices.content: \(a\) and \(c\) intersect but are not perpendicular.

question.prompt: In the same plane, \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are three distinct lines. If \(a\perp b\) and \(b\perp c\), what is the positional relationship between \(a\) and \(c\)?

solutions.explanation: Both \(a\) and \(c\) are perpendicular to \(b\). In the same plane, two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel to each other, so \(a\parallel c\).
solutions.title: Use the common perpendicular
